title: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Crescent Energy, Devon Energy, Energy Transfer, Cenovus Energy and Drilling Tools International
author: Zacks.Com
description: Energy sector M&A activity is accelerating with elevated crude prices around $90/barrel supporting strategic acquisitions. Crescent Energy is acquiring Devon Energy's Eagle Ford assets for $3.85 billion, Energy Transfer is acquiring Vaquero Midstream for $2.63 billion, Cenovus Energy is acquiring Athabasca Oil for C$5.7 billion, and Drilling Tools International is acquiring Saltire and Foxley for approximately $80 million in cash and stock. These transactions are expected to enhance operational efficiency, expand production capacity, and generate significant synergies for the acquiring companies.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Acquiring Devon Energy's Eagle Ford assets for $3.85 billion will add 68,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, position it as the basin's second-largest operator, generate $140 million in annual synergies by 2027, and enhance capital efficiency. Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) rating supports positive outlook.

Divesting Eagle Ford assets to Crescent Energy; while this represents a strategic divestment, the article does not provide specific sentiment indicators about the impact on Devon Energy's overall position or future prospects.

Acquiring Vaquero Midstream for $2.63 billion strengthens natural gas gathering and processing operations in the Delaware Basin with 300-mile pipeline network and 675 million cubic feet per day capacity. Fee-based contracts averaging 10 years are expected to immediately increase distributable cash flow per common unit.

Acquiring Athabasca Oil for C$5.7 billion adds 45,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day and substantial long-life reserves. Management plans to increase thermal oil production to 115,000 barrels per day by 2032 with C$85 million in annual synergies. Zacks Rank #1 rating supports positive outlook.

Acquiring Saltire and Foxley for approximately $80 million in cash and 17.4 million shares significantly expands international presence, increasing Eastern Hemisphere contribution from 18% to 40% of revenues. Expected to generate $50.4 million in annualized revenues and improve EBITDA margins.
